name: Padikasu Nathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the Tevaram hymns, with a 9th-century Chola masonry structure later expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks. The village is remembered as the birthplace of Pugalthunai Nayanar, one of the 63 Nayanmars.
story: Shiva is said to have left a gold coin (padikasu) each day for the poor devotee Pugazh Thunai who kept serving the deity through a famine.

name: Sivagurunathaswamy Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam mentioned in the 7th-century Tevaram canon, originally raised by the Cholas with the present masonry structure built under the 16th-century Nayaks. Sivapuram village near Kumbakonam is known chiefly for this shrine.
story: Tradition holds that Surya, Chandra, Brahma and Vishnu in his boar form all worshipped the deity at this site.

name: Sarguna Lingeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Sarguna Lingeswarar (sand Prithvi linga)
significance: Also known as Karukudi Nathar Temple, this shrine near Kumbakonam was sung by the saint Sambandar in the Tevaram; its main icon is a shivalinga of sand. Pilgrims traditionally seek relief here from skin ailments.
story: A trader named Dhananjayan is said to have been cured of leprosy at this place.

name: Vanchinadha Swamy Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams revered in the Tevaram, with an 11th-century Chola masonry structure expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks in the 16th century.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared as Vanchinathar at the village border to halt Yama when the god of death pursued a sage doing penance here.

name: Madhuvaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Nannilam town praised by the saint Sambandar in the Tevaram; its construction is traditionally attributed to the Early Chola king Kocengannan.
story: The temple town's name is traced to a forest of madhu trees believed to have once covered the region.

name: Soundareswararswamy Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, centred on a sacred palmyra tree and associated with the Early Chola king Karikala.
story: Karikala is said to have been standing under the temple's palmyra tree when the royal elephant identified him as king, leading to his coronation.

name: Veerateeswarar Temple, Thiruvirkudi
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by Sambandar and one of the eight Ashta Veeratta Sthalams marking Shiva's victories over demons; the present masonry structure dates to the 9th-century Cholas with Nayak-era expansions.
story: Shiva is said to have manifested here as Veerateeswarar to destroy the demon Jalandhara, who had been born of the fire of Shiva's third eye cast into the ocean.

name: Vardhamaneswarar Temple (Tiruppugalur Vardhamaneeswaram)
deity: Shiva as Vardhamaneswarar / Konal Piran (consort Karunthazhkuzhali)
significance: Counted separately among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams though it shares its precinct with the Agnipureeswarar temple of Tiruppugalur; it was praised by Sambandar. Its linga is known as the Konal (skewed) lingam for its tilted form.

name: Ramanathaswami Temple (Ramanadeeswaram)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, located between Tiruvarur and Mayiladuthurai and linked in tradition with Rama's worship of Shiva.
story: Rama is believed to have worshipped Shiva here, as at Rameswaram, to absolve himself of the sin of killing Ravana.

name: Tirupayatrunathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of the saint Tirunavukkarasar (Appar).

name: Uthirapasupatheeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Uthirapasupatheeswarar (consort Vaaitha Tirukuzhal Umai Nayaki)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, sung by both Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar; the place was historically known as Ganapatheesaram.

name: Rathnagiriswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, its glories sung by the saints Appar and Tirugnana Sambandar.
story: The village is said to take its name from a marugal plantain growing since time immemorial on the northern side of the temple.

name: Ayavandeeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, and also counted among the Vaippu Sthalams mentioned by Appar.

name: Kayarohanaswami Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in existence since the 6th century CE and rebuilt by the Pallavas, Cholas and Vijayanagara kings; it is linked to the Lakulisha tradition and houses a Thyagaraja image of lapis lazuli.
story: A Chola king, Mucukunta, is said to have won seven Thyagaraja images from Indra, installed across the Cauvery delta as the Saptha Vidangam shrines whose deities dance in procession.

name: Sikkal Navaneetheswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; the complex also holds the well-known Singaravelan (Murugan) shrine.

name: Keezhvelur Kediliappar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram; its sculptures and mentions in old Saiva literature are held to show an age of a thousand years or more.

name: Deva Pureeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, traditionally visited by the unmarried and by couples praying for children.
story: Kubera is said to have worshipped Shiva here to recover wealth stolen by Ravana, and the Devas to be absolved of slaying Vruddhasura.

name: Tirunethranathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, celebrated in the Tevaram verses of the saint Tirunavukkarasar.

name: Araneri Achaleswarar Temple
significance: A shrine within the precincts of the great Thyagaraja temple of Tiruvarur that is counted separately among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified by the saint Tirunavukkarasar.

name: Thyagaraja Temple, Tiruvarur
deity: Shiva as Thyagarajaswami / Putridankondar (consorts Neelotpalambika and Kamalambika)
significance: One of India's largest temple complexes at 8.1 hectares with nine gopurams and Asia's heaviest processional chariot, and a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the Tevaram. Believed to have been initiated by the Pallavas in the 7th century, the present masonry structure was built by the 9th-century Cholas, and it heads the seven Saptha Vidangam shrines.
story: King Muchukunda is said to have won from Indra the image of Shiva dancing on Vishnu's chest by correctly choosing it among seven identical icons.

name: Thoovanayanar Thoovainathar Temple (Paravai Un Mandali)
significance: A shrine on Tiruvarur's East Street, historically called Arurparavaiyunmandazhi, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and glorified by Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Vilamal Pathanchali Manoharar Temple
deity: Shiva as Pathanchali Manoharar (consort Yazhinum Menmozhiyaal)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Karavera Nathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams with hymns by the Tevaram poet-saints; unmarried women traditionally visit seeking blessings for marriage.

name: Tirupperuvelur Abhimuktheeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram by both Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar; the site is also known as Tirupperuvelur.

name: Nardana Pureeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam praised by the saint Tirunavukkarasar; prayer here is traditionally believed to cure leprosy.
story: The Pandya king Nedunchezhiyan is believed to have defeated the Chera and Chola kings at this place.

name: Koneswarar Temple, Kudavasal
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, built as an elevated maadakkovil attributed to the Early Chola king Kochengat Chola before 660 CE; it has an 80-foot rajagopuram and two prakarams.
story: During the great deluge, the lid of Brahma's pot holding the seeds of all living beings is said to have come to rest at this spot.

name: Tirucherai Gnanaparameswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, where the Nayanmars Appar and Sambandar sang in praise of the deity.
story: The sage Markandeya, the river-goddess Kaveri and the rishi Dowmya are said to have worshipped Shiva at this shrine.

name: Apatsahayesvarar Temple, Alangudi
deity: Shiva as Apathsahyesvarar (consort Elavarkuzhali); Guru (Jupiter) shrine
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the Tevaram and one of Tamil Nadu's nine Navagraha pilgrimage temples, honoured as the Guru (Jupiter) sthalam. The original complex is credited to the Cholas, with the present masonry built under the 16th-century Nayaks.
story: Shiva is said to have drunk the deadly poison of the ocean-churning here, earning the name Apatsahayesvarar, the saviour in peril.

name: Aridwaramangalam Padaleswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, and one of the five Pancha Aranya (forest) Sthalams of the Kumbakonam-Tiruvarur region.
story: Shiva is said to have hidden underground before his wedding, and Vishnu, as a boar, dug a doorway to find him, giving the place the name Haridwara, Hari's door.

name: Avalivanallur Satchinathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram, and part of the Pancha Aranya (five forest) Sthalams cluster of the Kumbakonam-Tiruvarur region.

name: Paridiniyamam Parithiappar Temple
significance: One of the Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; the temple marks the spot where the sun god is believed to have worshipped Shiva, giving the place its name.
story: Surya, the sun god, is said to have worshipped Shiva at this site.

name: Venni Karumbeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the Tevaram; devotees traditionally offer sugar to the deity seeking a cure for diabetes.
story: The main linga is shaped like a bundle of sugarcane stems tied together, karumbu being Tamil for sugarcane.

name: Chathuranga Vallabhanathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, praised by Sambandar; the temple is traditionally frequented by asthma patients seeking relief.
story: A childless king, Vasudevan, lost a game of chess to Shiva disguised as a siddha, after which Parvati was born to him as the princess Rajarajeswari.

name: Parijatha Vaneswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Parijatha Vaneswarar / Kalarmulainathar (consort Amudhavalli)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams with Tevaram hymns by Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar, marked by an 80-foot five-tiered east-facing rajagopuram.
story: The sage Durvasa is said to have brought parijatha flowers from the celestial world and installed a shivalinga beneath a parijatha tree in the grove he planted here.

name: Ponvaithanathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, celebrated in the Tevaram hymns of the saints Appar and Sundarar.

name: Tiruvusaattaanam Mandirapureeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Sarguna Nathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams with hymns by Sambandar, traditionally visited by devotees seeking freedom from the fear of death.
story: Yama, the god of death, is said to have worshipped Shiva here to atone for trying to carry off the sage Markandeya.

name: Karpaganatharkulam Karpaganathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; its main shivalinga is unusual for its hexagonal shape.

name: Kottur Kozhundeeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; the place was historically known as Indirapuram.

name: Vandurai Nathar Temple
deity: Shiva as Vandurai Nathar (consort Vel Nedunganni)
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, with Tevaram hymns composed by the saint Sambandar.
story: The sage Brungi, cursed by Parvati for honouring only Shiva, is said to have become a bee and entered the deity's idol here.

name: Tirukkollampudur Vilvaranyeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, and one of the five Pancha Aranya (forest) Sthalams, associated with the vilva grove.

name: Pereyil Jagadeeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, celebrated in the Tevaram by the saint Tirunavukkarasar; the site's historical name is Pereyil, and the shrine stands in Tirukkollampudur village.

name: Tirukkollikkadu Agneeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Agneeswarar (consort Panjin Melladi Ammai)
significance: The 115th of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar; worship here is believed to burn away obstacles and bring good fortune.

name: Thiruthangur Vellimalainathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Tirunellikka Nellivananathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram verses of Tirugnanasambandar.
